sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Tottenham host Leeds at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium with both clubs still looking to secure safety. The model gives Tottenham a slight edge (home win 42%, draw 25%, away win 33) and rates both teams to score at 57%. League table: Tottenham 17th (37 points), Leeds 16th (43).

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Tottenham are unbeaten in 3 (W2, D1) after back‑to‑back away wins at Aston Villa and Wolverhampton, with expected goals near 1.0 in each. Leeds have 3 wins in their last 5 and took 4 points from their last 3 away matches (win at Manchester United, draw at Bournemouth).

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Tottenham have won the last 2 meetings and 5 in a row overall. Recent matchups have consistently produced goals, with both sides often finding the net.

sections.subtitle: Season stats snapshot
sections.text: Tottenham: 45 scored, 54 conceded; goals vs expected goals difference -8.65; clean sheets 8; tackles per game 19.6 (1st); yellow cards 91 (most). Leeds: 47 scored, 52 conceded; a large share of their goals arrive late (76–90 minutes: 28%).

sections.subtitle: Tactics and key players
sections.text: Tottenham’s wide delivery is a key route (165 accurate crosses; 13 headers scored, rank 2). Richarlison leads with 10 goals, while Pedro Porro drives progression from right‑back. Leeds’ focal points are Dominic Calvert‑Lewin (12 goals) and Anton Stach (5 goals, 3 assists), with Ethan Ampadu anchoring midfield. Notable absences: Tottenham without Xavi Simons and Mohammed Kudus; Leeds without Noah Okafor.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee Jarred Gillett averages 4.0 yellow cards per game. Tottenham commit many fouls (417) and average 2.6 yellow cards per game, so an above‑average card count is likely. Corners profile points to a double‑digit total given Tottenham’s 5.26 corners per game and both teams’ recent trends.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Leeds arrive in better overall momentum, but Tottenham’s recent uptick and strong head‑to‑head record narrow the gap. With the model giving a home edge and both teams to score at 57%, the lean is Tottenham to edge a close game with both teams on the scoresheet.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Goalless at the break at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, with Tottenham Hotspur on top territorially and creating the clearer looks. Tottenham lead possession and territory, while Leeds United have stayed compact, defended their box well and carried a threat from set-pieces and quick breaks.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical flow and attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Leeds began with a brief early push before Tottenham took control from around the 7th minute, sustaining pressure for most of the half. There was a short Leeds spell midway through, but Tottenham reasserted themselves with repeated waves up to the interval. Leeds fashioned their best moments from transitions and dead balls, while Tottenham’s most dangerous phases came from sustained right-sided pressure and quick combinations around the box.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key statistics snapshot
halftimeSections.text: Tottenham lead possession (62%), expected goals (0.82 to 0.14), shots on target (2 to 1), corners (6 to 1) and penalty area entries (22 to 8). Leeds lead aerial duels (71% to 29%) and recorded the only woodwork hit. Both sides created 1 big chance and missed 1.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Player notes
halftimeSections.text: For Tottenham, Pedro Porro has been influential with 2 key passes and a shot on target, Rodrigo Bentancur has arrived in good areas, and Richarlison missed the clearest Tottenham chance. Destiny Udogie’s defensive work has been tidy. For Leeds, Brenden Aaronson created their best opening and worked hard out of possession, Joe Rodon threatened from a set-piece and registered the big miss, Jaka Bijol has made several clearances, and Daniel James has supported defensively.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Discipline and set-pieces
halftimeSections.text: Tottenham have 1 yellow card (Kevin Danso), Leeds have none. Tottenham’s 6 first-half corners and Leeds’ advantage in aerial duels point to set-pieces remaining decisive. Expect Tottenham to continue forcing corners, while Leeds’ main threat looks like near-post and back-post deliveries and second balls. A tight scoreline and frequent duels suggest a possibility of a couple more cautions after the interval.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: Tottenham’s control of territory, penalty area entries and chance quality suggests they are likelier to score first after the restart. To break Leeds down, Tottenham should vary deliveries away from high aerial contests and target cut-backs and low crosses, especially through Porro’s channel. Leeds’ route back into the game is through set-pieces and quick counters into space, with direct balls and knockdowns potentially testing Tottenham’s centre-backs, particularly with the booking in the home back line.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Tottenham to edge a tight game. The next goal is more likely to be scored by Tottenham, with Richarlison the most probable scorer given his first-half involvement. Leeds remain live from set-pieces, but Tottenham’s sustained pressure should tell.
